newsitem.title: USA: Scientific in Fla. energy monitoring pact.
newsitem.headline: Scientific in Fla. energy monitoring pact.

text.p: Scientific-Atlanta Inc said Monday it signed a contract with Gulf Power Co to provide and manage utility-monitoring and energy management systems in the homes of Gulf Power customers in Florida.
Scientific-Atlanta's "MainGate" system will be installed in about 40,000 homes in northwestern Florida over the next seven to eight years, beginning in May 1997, the company said.
Gulf Power is a subsidiary of Atlanta-based Southern Co.
The MainGate system is built around an open architecture and supports a variety of communications protocols and media, including Lonworks, CEBus, RF and hardwire.
The MainGate communications system links customers via a VHF paging interface, with a telephone line response back to the utility.

It lets customers program major appliances, such as heat-and-air conditioning systems, water heaters and pool pumps, to respond to external control from the utility company based on different pricing tiers.
Additional services that Gulf Power may decide to offer include outage detection, surge suppression and monitoring, and, in the future, home security and home automation, Scientific-American said.
The two-way interactive system also enables Gulf Power to remotely read meters and detect certain forms of meter tampering, the company said.
The contract covers an eight-year period.
